title: Don’t Bring Up AI if You Want to Enjoy Your Thanksgiving
gist: AI has become a new intergenerational flashpoint at family gatherings: young adults facing a weak entry-level job market and creatives whose work trained models clash with older relatives who see AI as benign or useful. A therapist frames it as a proxy fight over economic grievance, and Pew/Axios data show under-30s are both more worried about AI and still heavy users.

insights.claim: Psychologist Matt Lundquist of Tribeca Therapy reports that arguments over AI are on the rise, especially within families, calling it 'the latest generational beef.'
insights.speaker: Elana Klein
insights.so_what: AI is becoming a cultural-identity issue, raising the risk of consumer and political backlash against AI products.

insights.claim: A Pew survey published in August found a majority of US adults under 30 are more concerned than excited about AI, and 73 percent of that group believe AI will result in fewer jobs.
insights.speaker: Elana Klein
insights.so_what: Strong youth job-loss fear is a political tailwind for AI labor regulation and a brand risk for AI firms.
insights.locator: This tracks with research from Pew

insights.claim: Despite their anxiety, young people still use AI: an Axios poll in August found 61 percent of 18-to-34-year-olds had used ChatGPT in the past month, 48 percent Gemini and 20 percent Claude.
insights.speaker: Elana Klein
insights.so_what: Usage share data: ChatGPT leads, Gemini a strong second, Claude a distant third among young adults — concern is not translating into abstention.
insights.locator: At the same time, young people are still using AI

insights.claim: Lundquist argues older, asset-rich adults are 'clueless' about how threatening AI feels to younger relatives because they own homes with low-rate mortgages and have finished paying for college.
insights.speaker: Elana Klein
insights.so_what: AI attitudes are splitting along asset ownership and career stage, mirroring broader housing/wealth-gap politics.
insights.quote: if you own your second or third home with a 2.8 percent interest rate and you've already sent your kids to college, you're not worried about this stuff
insights.locator: Lundquist has found that many older adults

insights.claim: Lundquist frames family AI fights as proxies for deeper economic grievance by young people over what previous generations left them and a world that no longer rewards expected paths.
insights.speaker: Elana Klein
insights.so_what: Anti-AI sentiment is partly an expression of generational economic frustration, so it may persist regardless of AI's actual performance.
insights.quote: I’m mad about the pittance you and your generation have left for me.
insights.locator: If you do decide to go at it

insights.claim: Young adults entering a difficult entry-level job market, such as a 23-year-old sports-media graduate struggling to find work, are clashing with parents who see AI as the next big step for everyone.
insights.speaker: Elana Klein
insights.so_what: Weak entry-level hiring is being attributed to AI by young workers, amplifying anti-AI sentiment.

insights.claim: Creative professionals are angered that AI models were trained on their uncredited, uncompensated work; a romance novelist learned one of her books was used to train AI models and confronted a relative praising ChatGPT.
insights.speaker: Elana Klein
insights.so_what: Copyright grievance among creators remains a persistent legal and reputational overhang for model developers.
insights.quote: ChatGPT is not a magical device? It is being created by pirating work from actual writers.

insights.claim: Older users are adopting AI for practical work and household tasks — managing chemical-plant data, designing a backyard, building infant feeding schedules — which younger relatives see as displacing paid creative and professional work.
insights.speaker: Elana Klein
insights.so_what: Shows AI adoption broadening among older, higher-income consumers, substituting for paid services.
insights.locator: When Kaleigh last returned to her parents’ house

insights.claim: Some committed anti-AI consumers actively opt out, appending 'minus AI' to Google searches and deactivating Microsoft Copilot, motivated by concerns over cognition, AI leaders' alignment with the Trump administration, and data-center water use.
insights.speaker: Elana Klein
insights.so_what: A niche but vocal opt-out segment ties AI to politics and environmental justice — fuel for data-center siting opposition.
insights.locator: Sophie has never used ChatGPT or Claude

insights.claim: An anti-AI interviewee described a relative switching from ChatGPT to Claude as picking 'the better-branded version of the same evil tool,' indicating Anthropic's brand reads as more palatable to some AI-skeptical users.
insights.speaker: Elana Klein
insights.so_what: Brand differentiation between AI labs is visible to consumers, even critics.
insights.quote: a total white-liberal move to pick the better-branded version of the same evil tool
